parole.testo: From a conflation of two suffixes Proto-Slavic *-ьka and Proto-Slavic *-ъka. The former always came to be used after velars (hence the occurrence of the Slavic first palatalization), while the latter always came to be used after -л- (hence the lack of palatalization of -л- before -ка).
Borrowed from Italian abbate, or Middle High German abbāt, from Latin abbās (“abbot”), oblique stem abbat-. Further (via Ancient Greek ἀββα (abba) and Aramaic אבא) from Proto-Semitic *ʔabw-.
From German Abonnent, either directly or perhaps via Polish abonent.

Borrowed either from Tatar алты (altı, “six”), referring to six dengas (six half-kopeks), or from Tatar алтын (altın, “gold”). These small coins were never minted in gold; however, compare to the semantic evolution of Latin solidus from a Roman gold coin to a medieval silver shilling.
Borrowed from German annoncieren, French annoncer.

parole.significato: grandiose (large and impressive, in size, scope or extent)
parole.testo: Per Shansky, probably an adapted borrowing of French grandiose + -ный (-nyj). Per Vasmer, from either German grandios or Italian grandioso. Compare Ukrainian грандіо́зний (hrandióznyj), Belarusian грандыёзны (hrandyjózny).

parole.significato: churl, boor, cad, chuff, vulgarian, bounder (rude and mean fellow)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Polish grubian(in), or from Czech hrubián, from German Grobian (“brute”), influenced by грубый (grubyj).

Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic искусьство (iskusĭstvo), which was either inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьzkusьstvo, or an inner formation from искоусъ (iskusŭ, “test, experiment”) + -ство (-stvo).

From German Koloss m and/or French colosse m, from Latin colossus m, from Ancient Greek κολοσσός m (kolossós).

parole.significato: coffee (in the form of a beverage)
parole.testo: First attested in late 17th or early 18th century. Borrowed from a West Germanic language, either English coffee, German Koffee, or directly from Dutch koffie, Ultimately from Italian caffè, from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of кафе́ (kafé).

parole.significato: poker (metal rod for adjusting burning logs or coals in a fire)

parole.significato: valve (a ball valve, a plug valve, or similar rotating device controlling flow through a pipe)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Dutch kraan or from Low German kran. Cognate to German Kran (“crane”).

parole.significato: crystal (a solid composed of an array of atoms with a periodic structure)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Kristall or French cristal, from Latin crystallum, from Ancient Greek κρύσταλλος (krústallos). Doublet of хруста́ль (xrustálʹ), which entered the Russian language via Byzantine Greek.

Inherited from Old East Slavic посълъ (posŭlŭ), from Proto-Slavic *posъlъ. Probably originally deverbal from the ancestor of посла́ть (poslátʹ), or alternatively from Proto-Slavic *po- + the deverbal form of *sъlati.
